claim: In 2021, 247 million people were diagnosed with malaria with over 619,000 people succumbing to the disease.
source: In 2021, 247 million people were diagnosed with malaria with over 619,000 people succumbing to the disease (WHO, 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to WHO, 2021.

claim: Mosquito and parasite strains resistant to insecticide-treated nets and antimalarial compounds have emerged.
source: Although insecticide-treated nets and various antimalarial compounds have aided in controlling the spread and combating severe clinical complications of the disease, mosquito and parasite strains resistant to such interventions have emerged (Wicht et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Wicht et al., 2020.

claim: The life cycle of Plasmodium spp. can be categorized into three distinct stages: the pre-erythrocytic, asexual blood stage, and sexual stages.
source: The life cycle of Plasmodium spp. can be categorized into three distinct stages: the pre-erythrocytic, asexual blood stage, and sexual stages.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the Plasmodium life cycle.

claim: Each stage of the Plasmodium life cycle features the parasite undergoing large-scale morphological changes accompanied by modifications in proteomic expression profiles.
source: Each step features the parasite undergoing large-scale morphological changes accompanied by modifications in proteomic expression profiles – with several proteins being exclusively expressed in a single stage (Florens et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Florens et al., 2002.

claim: Several Plasmodium proteins are exclusively expressed in a single stage of the parasite life cycle.
source: Each step features the parasite undergoing large-scale morphological changes accompanied by modifications in proteomic expression profiles – with several proteins being exclusively expressed in a single stage (Florens et al., 2002).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Florens et al., 2002.

claim: RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M are the only two malaria vaccines recommended by the World Health Organization.
source: The pre-erythrocytic stage – following the transmission of sporozoites to humans by a bite from an infected mosquito – is a bottleneck targeted by the only two malaria vaccines recommended by the World Health Organization, RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M (Laurens, 2020; Datoo et al., 2024).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Laurens, 2020 and Datoo et al., 2024.

claim: RTS,S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines are based on the circumsporozoite protein (CSP).
source: The vaccines are based on the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) – an essential protein expressed at high density on the surface of the parasite during the pre-erythrocytic stage (Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997.

claim: CSP is an essential protein expressed at high density on the surface of the parasite during the pre-erythrocytic stage.
source: The vaccines are based on the circumsporozoite protein (CSP) – an essential protein expressed at high density on the surface of the parasite during the pre-erythrocytic stage (Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cerami et al., 1992; Frevert et al., 1993; Ménard et al., 1997.

claim: CSP contains various four amino acid repeat motifs in its central domain, with NANP repeats being the most predominant.
source: In its central domain, the protein contains various four amino acid repeat motifs – the most predominant of those being NANP repeats.
evidence: This is established knowledge about CSP structure.

claim: Protective antibodies elicited against CSP primarily target the immunodominant repeat region.
source: Protective antibodies elicited against CSP primarily target this immunodominant repeat region.
evidence: This is established knowledge about anti-CSP antibody responses.

claim: A large proportion of anti-CSP antibodies engage in homotypic interactions characterized by direct interactions between two antibodies' variable regions when bound to adjacent repetitive epitopes.
source: A large proportion of these antibodies engage in homotypic interactions which are characterized by direct interactions between two antibodies' variable regions when bound to adjacent repetitive epitopes (Kucharska et al., 2022a; Kucharska et al., 2022b; Imkeller et al., 2018; Martin et al., 2023b; Pholcharee et al., 2021; Oyen et al., 2018; Martin et al., 2023a; Murugan et al., 2020; Tripathi et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Homotypic interactions have been demonstrated to augment B cell activation and contribute to shaping the humoral response to CSP.
source: Such interactions have been demonstrated to augment B cell activation and contribute to shaping the humoral response to CSP (Imkeller et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Imkeller et al., 2018.

claim: First-generation malaria vaccines only induce short-lived efficacy in a subset of the at-risk population.
source: Although these first-generation malaria vaccines only induce short-lived efficacy in a subset of the at-risk population (RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership, 2015), they will undoubtedly assist in lowering the overall incidence of malaria in young infants with clear initial impact (Wadman, 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to RTS,S Clinical Trials Partnership, 2015.

claim: Combining multiple types of interventions that target different stages of the Plasmodium life cycle may strongly increase the efficacy of weaker interventions.
source: Modeling suggests that for improvements toward eradication of the disease, combining multiple types of interventions that target different stages of the Plasmodium life cycle may strongly increase the efficacy of weaker interventions (Golumbeanu et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Golumbeanu et al., 2022.

claim: Intraerythrocytic Plasmodium gametocytes are capable of eliciting antibody responses through clearance in the spleen.
source: This stage begins when intraerythrocytic Plasmodium gametocytes, which are capable of eliciting antibody responses through clearance in the spleen (Stone et al., 2016), are taken up through a mosquito blood meal.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stone et al., 2016.

claim: Transmission-blocking vaccines (TBVs) aim to elicit antibodies that target sexual stage antigens to block the reproduction of the parasite in the mosquito.
source: Vaccines that aim to target this life cycle bottleneck are known as transmission-blocking vaccines (TBVs) (Nikolaeva et al., 2015; Duffy, 2021). The goal of TBVs is to elicit antibodies that target sexual stage antigens to block the reproduction of the parasite in the mosquito and thus onward transmission to humans.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Nikolaeva et al., 2015 and Duffy, 2021.

claim: Current TBV development efforts are primarily focused on two antigens, Pfs230 and Pfs48/45.
source: Current TBV development efforts are primarily focused on two antigens, Pfs230 and Pfs48/45, as they are the targets of the most potent transmission-blocking antibodies identified to date (Roeffen et al., 2001; Ivanochko et al., 2023; Fabra-García et al., 2023; Kundu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Pfs230 and Pfs48/45 are the targets of the most potent transmission-blocking antibodies identified to date.
source: Current TBV development efforts are primarily focused on two antigens, Pfs230 and Pfs48/45, as they are the targets of the most potent transmission-blocking antibodies identified to date (Roeffen et al., 2001; Ivanochko et al., 2023; Fabra-García et al., 2023; Kundu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Individuals with sera enriched in antibodies that target Pfs230 and Pfs48/45 were found to have high transmission-reducing activity (TRA).
source: Indeed, individuals with sera enriched in antibodies that target Pfs230 and Pfs48/45 were found to have high transmission-reducing activity (TRA) (Stone et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stone et al., 2018.

claim: Sera depleted in antibodies targeting the pro-domain and domain 1 of Pfs230 and domains 2 and 3 of Pfs48/45 can retain TRA while maintaining the ability to recognize the surface of parasites lacking Pfs48/45 and Pfs230 surface expression.
source: However, sera depleted in antibodies targeting the pro-domain and domain 1 of Pfs230 and domains 2 and 3 of Pfs48/45 can retain TRA while maintaining the ability to recognize the surface of parasites lacking Pfs48/45 and Pfs230 surface expression (Stone et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stone et al., 2018.

claim: A workflow was designed for the isolation of antibodies to sexual stage-specific antigens from a donor who was repeatedly exposed to malaria parasites.
source: We designed a workflow for the isolation of antibodies to sexual stage-specific antigens from a donor who was repeatedly exposed to malaria parasites.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the study's methodology.

claim: The study yielded a panel of 14 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting Pfs230 and Pfs48/45 as well as other unidentified proteins, some with TRA.
source: Our efforts yielded a panel of 14 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) targeting Pfs230 and Pfs48/45 as well as other unidentified proteins, some with TRA.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the study's results.

claim: One mAb, B1E11K, was cross-reactive to various proteins containing glutamate-rich repetitive elements expressed at different stages of the parasite life cycle.
source: One mAb, B1E11K, was cross-reactive to various proteins containing glutamate-rich repetitive elements expressed at different stages of the parasite life cycle.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the study's findings.

claim: A crystal structure of two B1E11K Fab domains in complex with its main antigen, RESA, showed binding of B1E11K to a repeating epitope motif in a head-to-head conformation engaging in affinity-matured homotypic interactions.
source: A crystal structure of two B1E11K Fab domains in complex with its main antigen, RESA, expressed on asexual blood stages, showed binding of B1E11K to a repeating epitope motif in a head-to-head conformation engaging in affinity-matured homotypic interactions.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the study's structural findings.

claim: The mode of recognition of Pf proteins through homotypic interactions, previously described only for Pf circumsporozoite protein (PfCSP), extends to other repeats expressed across various stages.
source: Thus, this mode of recognition of Pf proteins, previously described only for Pf circumsporozoite protein (PfCSP), extends to other repeats expressed across various stages.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural data and comparison to previous findings.

claim: Donor A is a 69-year-old Dutch expatriate who resided in Central Africa for approximately 30 years.
source: We selected donor A, a 69-year-old Dutch expatriate who resided in Central Africa for approximately 30 years and whose serum was shown to strongly reduce Pf transmission, to isolate sexual stage-specific mAbs.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study donor.

claim: Donor A's serum was shown to strongly reduce Pf transmission.
source: We selected donor A, a 69-year-old Dutch expatriate who resided in Central Africa for approximately 30 years and whose serum was shown to strongly reduce Pf transmission, to isolate sexual stage-specific mAbs.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the donor's serum properties.

claim: The serum of donor A largely retained its TRA when depleted of antibodies directed against the main transmission-blocking epitopes of Pfs48/45 and Pfs230.
source: We previously demonstrated the serum of this donor, donor A, largely retained its TRA when depleted of antibodies directed against the main transmission-blocking epitopes of Pfs48/45 and Pfs230 (Stone et al., 2018), suggesting the presence of antibodies targeting other epitopes on these two proteins or directed at other proteins also involved in transmission.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stone et al., 2018.

claim: A total of 1496 IgG+ memory B cells were sorted from donor A's PBMCs in 384-well plates.
source: PBMCs from the donor were thawed and a total of 1496 IgG+ memory B cells were sorted in 384-well plates (Figure 1) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental procedure with reference to figures.

claim: Supernatants from 84 wells reacted with gamete and/or gametocyte lysate proteins, representing 5.6% of the total memory B cells.
source: In total, supernatants from 84 wells reacted with gamete and/or gametocyte lysate proteins, representing 5.6% of the total memory B cells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: Of the 21 supernatants screened against both gamete and gametocyte lysates, six recognized both, nine appeared to recognize exclusively gamete proteins, and six exclusively gametocyte proteins.
source: Of the 21 supernatants that were screened against both gamete and gametocyte lysates, six recognized both, while nine appeared to recognize exclusively gamete proteins, and six exclusively gametocyte proteins.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: Heavy and light chain sequences were obtained and cloned for 11 out of 84 ELISA-positive wells.
source: We obtained and cloned heavy and light chain sequences for 11 out of 84 wells.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: 14 mAbs were expressed as full human IgG1s.
source: Following amplification and cloning, 14 mAbs were expressed as full human IgG1s (Supplementary files 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental procedure.

claim: Seven mAbs exhibited binding to approximately half or more of wild-type female gametes when tested at a concentration of 100 µg/mL.
source: Seven mAbs exhibited binding to approximately half or more of gametes when tested at a concentration of 100 µg/mL.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Four mAbs, B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, and B2E9L, recognized wild-type gametes with high scores (>68%) even at concentrations as low as 1 µg/mL.
source: Among these, four mAbs, B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, and B2E9L, recognized wild-type gametes with high scores (>68%) even at concentrations as low as 1 µg/mL.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: The binding of B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, and B2E9L mAbs strongly decreased when using gametes that lacked surface-expressed Pfs48/45 and Pfs230.
source: The binding of the B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, and B2E9L mAbs strongly decreased when using gametes that lacked surface-expressed Pfs48/45 and Pfs230, indicating that these four mAbs likely targeted one of these two antigens.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: B1E11K exhibited a distinctive gamete surface binding profile, recognizing only a fraction (approximately a third to a fifth) of the wild-type and Pfs48/45 knockout gametes across all tested concentrations.
source: Finally, one mAb, B1E11K, exhibited a distinctive gamete surface binding profile, recognizing only a fraction (approximately a third to a fifth) of the wild-type and Pfs48/45 knockout gametes across all tested concentrations, suggesting potential binding to non-Pfs48/45 and Pfs230 proteins.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: Seven mAbs were confirmed to strongly reduce transmission (TRA>80%) when tested at 500 µg/ml: B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, B2E9L, B1C8L, B1D3L, and B1F9K.
source: Overall, seven mAbs were confirmed to strongly reduce transmission (TRA>80%) when tested at 500 µg/ml: B1C5K, B1C5L, B2C10L, B2E9L, B1C8L, B1D3L, and B1F9K.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Two mAbs, B1C8L and B2C10L, retained >50% TRA at a lower concentration (100 µg/ml).
source: Of those, two mAbs, B1C8L and B2C10L, retained >50% TRA at a lower concentration (100 µg/ml).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: B1F9K and B1D3L displayed TRA despite not showing gamete surface recognition.
source: Notably, despite not showing gamete surface recognition, B1F9K and B1D3L displayed TRA – although only at high concentrations.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: Three mAbs recognizing the gamete surface, B2D10L, B1E7K, and B1E11K, showed no activity in SMFA.
source: Conversely, three mAbs recognizing the gamete surface, B2D10L, B1E7K, and B1E11K, showed no activity in SMFA (Standard membrane feeding assay).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: B1C5K and B1C5L mAbs recognized a protein with a molecular weight matching that of Pfs48/45 in western blot.
source: The B1C5K and B1C5L mAbs recognized a protein with a molecular weight matching that of Pfs48/45.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: B2C10L mAb displayed a pattern of recognition that corresponded to Pfs230 in western blot.
source: The B2C10L mAb displayed pattern of recognition that corresponded to Pfs230, similar to the anti-Pfs230 control mAb RUPA-96 (Ivanochko et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to Figure 2C and a citation.

claim: B1E11K mAb appeared to bind to Pfs230 on the western blot, recognizing only the higher molecular band corresponding to the unprocessed form of this protein.
source: The B1E11K mAb also appeared to bind to Pfs230 on the western blot. However, in contrast to the RUPA-96 mAb, B1E11K only recognized the higher molecular band corresponding to Pfs230, suggesting exclusive recognition of the unprocessed form of this protein (Brooks and Williamson, 2000).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with a citation.

claim: B1E11K recognized several unidentified proteins ranging from 70 kDa and 250 kDa with various intensities in western blot.
source: Interestingly, besides Pfs230, B1E11K also recognized several unidentified proteins ranging from 70 kDa and 250 kDa with various intensities.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: The recognition of Pfs48/45 by B1C5K and B1C5L mAbs was confirmed through an ELISA using full-length recombinant Pfs48/45.
source: The recognition of Pfs48/45 by the B1C5K and B1C5L mAbs was subsequently confirmed through an ELISA using full-length recombinant Pfs48/45 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: B1C5K and B1C5L mAbs targeted domain 2 of Pfs48/45.
source: To further pinpoint the domain targeted by B1C5K and B1C5L, an ELISA was performed using constructs corresponding to domains 1–2, 2–3, and 3 revealing that these two mAbs targeted domain 2 of Pfs48/45 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: mAbs to domain 2 of Pfs48/45 are generally mAbs with low potency.
source: This is in agreement with prior work indicating mAbs to domain 2 of Pfs48/45 are generally mAbs with low potency (Fabra-García et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fabra-García et al., 2023.

claim: B2C10L mAb did not show reactivity to Pfs230CMB in ELISA.
source: We thus tested this mAb in ELISA for binding to Pfs230CMB, a construct containing Pfs230 domain 1 and part of the pro-domain (Farrance et al., 2011). No reactivity was observed (Figure 2F) suggesting that B2C10L may recognize other Pfs230 domains than the one tested, or recognize epitopes not properly displayed in the construct used.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: B1E11K mAb did not bind any of the antigens on the polyreactivity panel at any significant level, even at a high 50 µg/ml concentration.
source: The B1E11K mAb did not bind any of the antigens on the panel at any significant level, even at a high 50 µg/ml concentration, and therefore polyreactivity was ruled out (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis of B1E11K immunoprecipitate revealed recognition of Pfs230.
source: Mass spectrometry analysis of the corresponding gel slices revealed recognition of Pfs230, confirming the western blot results.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: B1E11K exhibited high level reactivity against several antigens on a protein microarray, including Pf11.1, LSA3, RESA, and RESA3.
source: The results showed that B1E11K exhibited high level reactivity (>8-fold higher than the negative control, minimum signal intensity rank 15th of 943 array targets) against several antigens, some expressed at the sexual stage (i.e. Pf11.1), others at the asexual stage (i.e. LSA3, RESA, RESA3) (Figure 3A; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: Analysis of the primary amino acid sequence of the antigens recognized by B1E11K in the array suggested homology based on the presence of glutamate-rich regions.
source: Analysis of the primary amino acid sequence of the antigens recognized in the array suggested homology in several cases, based on the presence of glutamate-rich regions (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the analysis results with reference to a figure.

claim: Pfs230, Pf11.1, RESA, RESA3, and LSA3 presented the most similar glutamate repeats, following an 'EE-XX-EE' pattern.
source: Among these proteins, Pfs230, Pf11.1, RESA, RESA3, and LSA3 presented the most similar glutamate repeats, following an 'EE-XX-EE' pattern (Figure 3—figure supplements 3 and 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis results with reference to figures.

claim: Pfs230 contains adjacent EE-VG-EE repeats which are located in the domain of the protein which is cleaved upon gametocyte egress from erythrocytes.
source: Pfs230 contains adjacent EE-VG-EE repeats which are located in the domain of the protein which is cleaved upon gametocyte egress from erythrocytes (Williamson et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Williamson et al., 1996.

claim: RESA contains 20 EE-NV-EE overlapping repeats at the C-terminus of the protein.
source: RESA and RESA3 contain 20 and 9 EE-NV-EE overlapping repeats at the C-terminus of the protein, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis results.

claim: RESA3 contains 9 EE-NV-EE overlapping repeats at the C-terminus of the protein.
source: RESA and RESA3 contain 20 and 9 EE-NV-EE overlapping repeats at the C-terminus of the protein, respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis results.

claim: LSA3 contains two overlapping EE-NV-EE repeats.
source: LSA3 contains two overlapping EE-NV-EE repeats.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis results.

claim: 221 non-adjacent EE-LV-EE repeats span the whole Pf11.1 megadalton protein.
source: Finally, 221 non-adjacent EE-LV-EE repeats span the whole Pf11.1 megadalton protein.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis results.

claim: Western blot confirmed the binding of B1E11K to recombinant forms of RESA, RESA3, LSA3, and a Pf11.1 domain.
source: To verify the recognition of the aforementioned proteins, a western blot was performed with recombinant forms of RESA, RESA3, LSA3, and of a Pf11.1 domain (de Jong, 2023; Figure 3B). Domain 1 of Pfs230, which does not contain the EE-VG-EE repeats, was also included. The results confirmed the binding of B1E11K to all the proteins tested except for Pfs230D1, as expected.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: B1E11K mAb bound to all five synthesized biotinylated peptides derived from glutamate-rich repeats.
source: Overall, the B1E11K mAb bound to all peptides (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure.

claim: B1E11K exhibited a higher specificity for the RESA-derived peptides with an EC50 at least 100 times greater compared to EC50 values obtained with the other glutamate-rich peptides.
source: However, it exhibited a higher specificity for the RESA-derived peptides with an EC50 at least 100 times greater compared to EC50 values obtained with the other glutamate-rich peptides.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: B1E11K mAb binding to RESA P2 (16AA), RESA 14AA, 12AA, and 10AA was similar, all exhibiting close EC50 values.
source: When tested on the RESA peptide panel, B1E11K mAb binding to RESA P2 (16AA) and RESA 14AA, 12AA, and 10AA was similar, all exhibiting close EC50 values (Figure 4B; Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: No binding was observed for the 8AA RESA peptide, suggesting the 10AA peptide contained the minimal epitope.
source: No binding was observed for the 8AA RESA peptide, suggesting the 10AA peptide contained the minimal epitope.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: B1E11K Fab bound both RESA P2 (16AA) and RESA 14AA peptides with comparable strength of binding.
source: Although B1E11K Fab bound both RESA P2 (16AA) and RESA 14AA peptides with comparable strength of binding, both RESA 12AA and RESA 10AA peptides displayed comparatively poorer EC50 values with the RESA 10AA peptide displaying the lowest detectable binding strength.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: An approximately six-fold difference in affinity was observed between the 10AA peptide (KD = 484 nM) and the P2 peptide (16AA) (KD = 74 nM) in BLI experiments.
source: When immobilizing the peptide to the sensors, an approximately six-fold difference in affinity between the 10AA peptide (KD = 484 nM) (Figure 4D) and the P2 peptide (16AA) (KD = 74 nM) (Figure 4E) was observed.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: ITC experiments showed a binding stoichiometry of N=1.0 ± 0.2 when titrating B1E11K Fab into RESA 10AA.
source: We observed when titrating the B1E11K Fab into RESA 10AA, a binding stoichiometry of N=1.0 ± 0.2 (Figure 4F; Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure and table.

claim: ITC experiments showed a stoichiometry of N=2.1 ± 0.1 when using the RESA P2 (16AA) peptide.
source: When using the RESA P2 (16AA) peptide, a stoichiometry of N=2.1 ± 0.1 was observed (Figure 4G; Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure and table.

claim: SEC-MALS experiments revealed two species eluted from the column, with the heavier species having a molecular weight in line with a 2:1 Fab:peptide complex (92 kDa).
source: The resulting chromatogram revealed two species eluted from the column. The molecular weight of the heavier species was in line with what would be expected from a 2:1 Fab:peptide complex (92 kDa) in which the mass determined fell within the range of experimental error.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: A negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM) map reconstruction of the 2:1 Fab:peptide complex permitted the fitting of two Fab molecules.
source: A negative-stain electron microscopy (nsEM) map reconstruction of the 2:1 Fab:peptide complex recovered from the SEC-MALS experiment (Figure 4H) permitted the fitting of two Fab molecules, further supporting the 2:1 binding model (Figure 4I).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to figures.

claim: A 2.6 Å crystal structure of the B1E11K:RESA P2 (16AA) peptide complex was solved.
source: To obtain a full structural understanding of the observed repeat cross-reactivity and selectivity for RESA exhibited by B1E11K, we solved a 2.6 Å crystal structure of the B1E11K:RESA P2 (16AA) peptide complex (Figure 5A; Table 2; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results with reference to a figure and table.

claim: The paratope of B1E11K is highly enriched in arginine and histidine residues giving rise to a highly electropositive groove.
source: The paratope of B1E11K is highly enriched in arginine and histidine residues giving rise to a highly electropositive groove (Figure 5B–D).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural analysis with reference to figures.

claim: B1E11K paratope residues form a plethora of salt-bridging interactions with the glutamate residue side chains of RESA repeats.
source: These residues form a plethora of salt-bridging interactions with the glutamate residue side chains of RESA repeats (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: Multiple hydrogen bonding interactions are made with B1E11K through the side chains of the asparagine residues of RESA repeats (EENV).
source: Multiple hydrogen bonding interactions are made with B1E11K through the side chains of the asparagine residues of RESA repeats (EENV) (Figure 5F) that would not exist in the context of binding to the repeats of Pf11.1 (EELV or EEVIP or EEFIP or EEVVP) or Pfs230 (EEVG) (Figure 3C), as these residues lack side chains that can form hydrogen bonds.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The hydrogen bonding interactions with asparagine residues likely lead to the observed higher specificity of B1E11K for RESA repeats.
source: This likely leads to the observed higher specificity of B1E11K for RESA repeats demonstrated in our ELISA experiments (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural analysis and experimental results.

claim: The crystal structure revealed the presence of homotypic antibody-antibody contacts through two interfaces surrounding the repeat peptide binding groove.
source: Additionally, the crystal structure of the antibody-antigen complex revealed the presence of homotypic antibody-antibody contacts through two interfaces surrounding the repeat peptide binding groove (Figure 5G; Figure 5—figure supplement 3; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The first homotypic interface features a salt-bridging network involving D60 of the Fab B kappa chain forming two salt bridges with R52 and H52A of the Fab A HCDR2.
source: The first interface features a salt-bridging network involving D60 of the Fab B kappa chain forming two salt bridges with R52 and H52A of the Fab A HCDR2 (Figure 5H).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The second homotypic interface features two hydrogen bonds between Y32 and S31 of the Fab B HCDR1 and the Fab A KCDR1 T29 and R27, respectively.
source: The second interface is less extensive featuring two hydrogen bonds between Y32 and S31 of the Fab B HCDR1 and the Fab A KCDR1 T29 and R27, respectively (Figure 5I).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the structural analysis with reference to a figure.

claim: The B1E11K heavy and light chain have high similarity to the IGHV3-7 and IGKV3-20 germline sequences.
source: Analysis of the B1E11K sequences with IgBLAST (Ye et al., 2013) reveals that the B1E11K heavy and light chain have high similarity to the IGHV3-7 and IGKV3-20 germline sequences (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: Multiple residues involved in the homotypic interaction interface have undergone somatic hypermutation.
source: This analysis also indicates multiple residues involved in the homotypic interaction interface have undergone somatic hypermutation.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the sequence analysis results.

claim: Repetitive regions rich in glutamate residues have been previously found to be highly immunogenic in malaria-experienced individuals.
source: Repetitive regions rich in glutamate residues have been previously found to be highly immunogenic in malaria-experienced individuals. A study investigating antibody responses against asexual stage antigens of Pf associated with erythrocyte invasion using sera from individuals from various cohorts found that the repetitive regions rich in glutamate residues within these antigens were predominantly recognized (Hou et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Hou et al., 2020.

claim: Antibodies that target glutamate-rich repeats may be potentially cross-reactive.
source: Another investigation into sera from individuals from Uganda corroborated this finding (Raghavan et al., 2023). Raghavan et al. noted the antibodies that target these repeats may be potentially cross-reactive but emphasized that such a claim could only be demonstrated by direct investigations into mAbs.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Raghavan et al., 2023.

claim: Only four mAbs that target glutamate-rich repeats have been described with their epitopes determined, of which three were obtained following mouse immunization and only one was of human origin.
source: To our knowledge, only four mAbs that target glutamate-rich repeats have been described in which their epitopes have been determined. Of those mAbs, three were obtained following mouse immunization, and only one was of human origin.
evidence: This is a statement based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: The murine mAb 1A1 recognizes Pf11.1-derived repeat peptides ([PEE(L/V)VEEV(I/V)]2).
source: The murine mAbs 1A1 (Feng et al., 1993) and 1E10 (Scherf et al., 1992) recognize Pf11.1-derived repeat peptides ([PEE(L/V)VEEV(I/V)]2);
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Feng et al., 1993.

claim: The murine mAb 1E10 recognizes Pf11.1-derived repeat peptides ([PEE(L/V)VEEV(I/V)]2).
source: The murine mAbs 1A1 (Feng et al., 1993) and 1E10 (Scherf et al., 1992) recognize Pf11.1-derived repeat peptides ([PEE(L/V)VEEV(I/V)]2);
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Scherf et al., 1992.

claim: The murine mAb 9B11 is able to bind to a peptide containing four EENV repeats of RESA.
source: the murine mAb 9B11 (Masuda et al., 1986) is able to bind to a peptide containing four EENV repeats of RESA;
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Masuda et al., 1986.

claim: The human mAb 33G2 is specific for a peptide repeat sequence found in Ag332 (VTEEI).
source: and finally the human mAb 33G2 (Udomsangpetch et al., 1986) is specific for a peptide repeat sequence found in Ag332 (VTEEI) (Ahlborg et al., 1991).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Udomsangpetch et al., 1986 and Ahlborg et al., 1991.

claim: Only the human mAb 33G2 appeared to exhibit cross-reactivity among the four mAbs targeting glutamate-rich repeats.
source: Despite all targeting linear epitopes containing tandem glutamate residues (EE), only 33G2 appeared to exhibit cross-reactivity (Udomsangpetch et al., 1989) and none had been structurally characterized.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Udomsangpetch et al., 1989.

claim: B cells expressing B cell receptors (BCRs) interacting via homotypic interactions activate more robustly in comparison to B cells that have mutated BCRs that disrupt this interaction.
source: We have previously shown that B cells expressing B cell receptors (BCRs) interacting via homotypic interactions activate more robustly in comparison to B cells that have mutated BCRs that disrupt this interaction (Imkeller et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Imkeller et al., 2018.

claim: Strong B cell activation mediated through the cross-linking of multiple BCRs at the B cell surface has been suggested to limit affinity maturation in germinal centers.
source: This strong B cell activation, presumably mediated through the cross-linking of multiple BCRs at the B cell surface (Clutterbuck et al., 2012), has been suggested to limit affinity maturation in germinal centers, potentially due to early exit of B cells, favoring the elicitation of short-term low-affinity antibodies to CSP over durable high-affinity responses, thus leading to suboptimal protective responses (Wahl and Wardemann, 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Clutterbuck et al., 2012 and Wahl and Wardemann, 2022.

claim: The phenomenon of limited affinity maturation may potentially be altered with the development of cross-reactive responses against repeats of slightly different content.
source: However, this phenomenon may potentially be altered with the development of cross-reactive responses against repeats of slightly different content (Murugan et al., 2020; Ludwig et al., 2023; Thai et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Murugan et al., 2020; Ludwig et al., 2023; Thai et al., 2023.

claim: Antibodies elicited against the repetitive elements described in this study have been demonstrated to be associated with a lower incidence of disease.
source: Indeed, antibodies elicited against the repetitive elements described here have been demonstrated to be associated with a lower incidence of disease (Riley et al., 1991; Petersen et al., 1990; Berzins et al., 1991) as well as disrupt the maturation of sexual stage parasites (Feng et al., 1993) in in vitro assays – although we note that mAb B1E11K isolated and characterized in this study did not show TRA.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Riley et al., 1991; Petersen et al., 1990; Berzins et al., 1991.

claim: Antibodies elicited against the repetitive elements described in this study have been demonstrated to disrupt the maturation of sexual stage parasites in in vitro assays.
source: Indeed, antibodies elicited against the repetitive elements described here have been demonstrated to be associated with a lower incidence of disease (Riley et al., 1991; Petersen et al., 1990; Berzins et al., 1991) as well as disrupt the maturation of sexual stage parasites (Feng et al., 1993) in in vitro assays – although we note that mAb B1E11K isolated and characterized in this study did not show TRA.
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Feng et al., 1993.

claim: mAb B1E11K isolated and characterized in this study did not show TRA.
source: Indeed, antibodies elicited against the repetitive elements described here have been demonstrated to be associated with a lower incidence of disease (Riley et al., 1991; Petersen et al., 1990; Berzins et al., 1991) as well as disrupt the maturation of sexual stage parasites (Feng et al., 1993) in in vitro assays – although we note that mAb B1E11K isolated and characterized in this study did not show TRA.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental results.

claim: Donor A had lived in Central Africa for approximately 30 years and reported multiple malaria infections during that period.
source: Donor A (Stone et al., 2018) had lived in Central Africa for approximately 30 years and reported multiple malaria infections during that period.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study donor with a citation.

claim: At the time of sampling PBMCs in 1994, donor A had recently returned to the Netherlands and visited the hospital with a clinical malaria infection.
source: At the time of sampling PBMCs, in 1994, donor A had recently returned to the Netherlands and visited the hospital with a clinical malaria infection.
evidence: This is a direct description of the study donor.

claim: The Pfs48/45 knockout lacks both surface-bound Pfs48/45 and Pfs230.
source: The Pfs48/45 knockout lacks both surface-bound Pfs48/45 and Pfs230 (Stone et al., 2018; Eksi et al., 2006; Kumar, 1987).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Stone et al., 2018; Eksi et al., 2006; Kumar, 1987.
